abstract.p: As a relatively new programming language, Rust has gained significant popularity in recent years due to its safety features during compilation. However, Rust developers often face challenges stemming from its strict compilation checks due to the steep learning curve of safety rules. To make matters worse, the lack of training data and the unique semantics of Rust lead to poor performance in learning-based automated program repair techniques. To address these challenges, we propose a novel error injection approach to generate a balanced training dataset and leverage the Mid-level Intermediate Representation (MIR) as enhanced features for Rust's unique compilation error repair. Using these innovations, we fine-tuned a new code model, LLaRRA: Large Language and Rust Repair Assistant. Experimental results demonstrate that LLaRRA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models in terms of Pass@K and Acc@K.
